summary: Iter29 testing complete. Backend: 22/22 pytest cases PASS covering adviser invite tokens, public invite preview (200/404/409 already_accepted), resend-invite rotation + already_linked 409, signup-with-invite auto-link, Document Vault CRUD (list/upload/get/download/patch/delete), send-to-decoder (wrong_category 400 + happy path with job polling), and adviser read-only access (?as_client_id 200 + non-adviser 403 + cross-adviser 404). Frontend: All required data-testids present and functional — adviser-invite-state-{id}='Invite pending', adviser-client-resend-{id} triggers POST /resend-invite and shows sonner toast 'Invite re-sent to ...', signup-invite-banner renders adviser name + notes and pre-fills name + email, /app/documents page renders 8 category pills (all + 7), upload works, docvault-card-{id} + Download/Edit/Delete buttons present, docvault-edit-modal + docvault-edit-save work, sidebar Documents link routes correctly.

ui_bugs.issue: React warning: 'Encountered two children with the same key' — month strings (May/Apr) being used as keys somewhere; non-unique. Multiple instances logged on /app/documents load.

issues: Linked column shows 'Invite pending' even for clients whose status is ACTIVE but who haven't yet linked a household (e.g., 'Invitee QA', 'Margaret Brown', 'Signup UI Test'). Copy is ambiguous — these clients have user accounts but no household. Consider 'Awaiting household onboarding' or 'User linked · household pending' for that intermediate state.

action_items: (Optional) Fix duplicate React key warning shown in console on /app/documents — likely a month-label key collision in a child component (e.g., Statements grouping or DocVault grouping). Use stable unique ids instead of period_label.
(Copy polish) On AdviserPortal, differentiate 'Invite pending' (no user yet) from 'User linked, household pending' for clients with linked_user_id but no linked_household_id.
critical_code_review_comments: documents_routes.py uses base64 storage in Mongo — fine for an MVP but will scale poorly past a few thousand docs per household. The MAX_VAULT_BYTES=100MB cap mitigates risk for now; consider GridFS or S3 in a later iter.

list_documents hard-codes `d['has_file']=True` after excluding file_b64 from projection. If a doc row was inserted without file_b64 it would incorrectly report has_file:true. Currently uploads always set file_b64 so safe in practice, but a defensive check on `file_size_bytes>0` would be cleaner.

Adviser invite email uses os.environ.get('PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN', 'https://wayly.com.au') — when running on the preview env, PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN is not set so invite links point to wayly.com.au instead of the preview URL. Not a blocker for prod, but means clicking the invite link from a real preview-env test email lands on the wrong host. Consider setting PUBLIC_APP_ORIGIN in preview backend/.env.

send-to-decoder happy path successfully kicked off an async job and the polling endpoint returned status='done' with a statement_id in ~15s. Document row's last_decoded_statement_id was updated. Working as designed.
